statement: One real sequence supported on J has exact mass P and takes values in [1/2,3/2] on J. The pooled squared discrepancy of the residue rows from P/k over k≤2K is O(PK), and the sum of the maximum absolute row discrepancies is O(K√P). On units the same orders hold about their induced means. The maximum-error budget is O_A(P/log^A T) for every fixed A. The unit-centered real projection against W(n)=Σ_(k∈S)(c_k/k)·1_((n,k)=1)·(cos(2πn/k)−μ(k)/φ(k)) is ≫|S|√T, exceeding T log⁴T by a divergent factor.
hypotheses: Fix 1/2<θ<2/3, K≍T^θ, integer P≍KT and J=[P,2P)∩ℤ. Take the primes in [X,(1+η)X] with X=K^(1/4) and fixed 0<η<2^(1/4)−1. Its full fourth-power support S⊂[K,2K) includes repeated factors, with |S|≍K/log⁴K and multinomial coefficients 1≤c_k≤24. The residue rows arise from one sequence and agree on marginals modulo common divisors. On units, the induced mean at each modulus is the total sequence mass on that modulus’s units divided by φ(k). This ordinary integer-interval setting leaves the prime-model P/φ(k) baseline, prime or sieve support, and the smooth C_* sum open.
